original.title: Classical Hodgkin-lymphoma clues
original.explanation: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma typically shows characteristic malignant cells, this immunophenotype, and an orderly lymph-node spread pattern.

entries.source: Bootcamp.com Hematology & Oncology.pdf; Leukemias and Lymphomas - Hodgkin Lymphoma; PDF p. 81

proposal.why: Breaks the CD15/CD30 pair that sorts mechanically; bimodal age distribution is a certain classical Hodgkin feature requiring recall.

entries.auditNote: Reed-Sternberg plus CD15/CD30 is a memorized triad.

revised.title: Classical Hodgkin-lymphoma clues
revised.explanation: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma typically shows Reed-Sternberg cells that express CD30, a bimodal age distribution, and orderly spread between contiguous lymph node groups.
revised.detail: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma is a B-cell neoplasm in which a few large malignant Reed-Sternberg cells (owl-eye nuclei) sit in a reactive inflammatory background. The tumor cells are typically CD15 and CD30 positive. Incidence peaks in young adults (about 20 to 30) and again in older adults (over about 55). Spread is usually contiguous from one nodal group to the next, unlike non-Hodgkin lymphoma, which more often spreads noncontiguously and involves extranodal sites. Nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma differs (CD20 positive, CD15 and CD30 negative popcorn cells).
tileNotes: Large binucleate or bilobed cells with prominent nucleoli (owl-eye appearance); the malignant cell of classical Hodgkin lymphoma.
Incidence peaks in young adults and again in older adults, a classic epidemiologic feature of Hodgkin lymphoma.
Reed-Sternberg cells express CD30 (the target of brentuximab vedotin), usually together with CD15.
Disease typically spreads in an orderly way to adjacent lymph node groups, which is the basis of staging and localized therapy.

entries.changeSummary: Replaced CD15 expression with Bimodal age distribution to break the CD15/CD30 pair.
entries.checkNote: Bimodal age distribution is a textbook classical Hodgkin feature and breaks the CD15/CD30 pair.

original.title: Burkitt-lymphoma clues
original.explanation: MYC-driven proliferation produces an aggressive lymphoma with classic histology and different common anatomic presentations by epidemiologic form.

entries.source: Bootcamp.com Hematology & Oncology.pdf; Leukemias and Lymphomas - Burkitt Lymphoma; PDF p. 82

proposal.why: Removes the paired endemic/sporadic involvement tiles; EBV association (especially endemic form) is certain.

entries.auditNote: Endemic jaw vs sporadic abdominal involvement is a memorized pair sharing the word involvement.

revised.title: Burkitt-lymphoma clues
revised.explanation: MYC-driven proliferation produces an aggressive B-cell lymphoma with starry-sky histology, a jaw-predominant endemic form, and a strong link to EBV.
revised.detail: Burkitt lymphoma is a high-grade B-cell lymphoma driven by MYC translocation, most often t(8;14) to the immunoglobulin heavy chain locus. Extremely rapid turnover gives a starry-sky pattern: sheets of tumor cells interspersed with macrophages that have engulfed apoptotic debris. The endemic (African) form typically involves the jaw and is almost always EBV positive, whereas the sporadic form usually presents in the abdomen (ileocecal region) and is less often EBV associated. Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma lacks the uniform starry-sky pattern and near 100% proliferation index.
tileNotes: Translocation of MYC on chromosome 8, usually t(8;14) with the IgH locus, drives uncontrolled proliferation.
Tingible body macrophages (the stars) scattered among sheets of dark tumor cells (the sky), reflecting high cell turnover.
The endemic African form characteristically presents as a jaw or facial mass in children.
EBV is found in nearly all endemic cases and a minority of sporadic cases.

entries.changeSummary: Replaced Sporadic abdominal involvement with EBV association to break the endemic/sporadic pairing.
entries.checkNote: EBV association is a standard Burkitt clue and the notes correctly separate endemic from sporadic EBV rates.

check.note: EBV association is a standard Burkitt clue and the notes correctly separate endemic from sporadic EBV rates.

original.title: Hairy-cell-leukemia clues
original.explanation: Classic hairy cell leukemia has characteristic morphology and molecular or cytochemical features, with marrow fibrosis that can impede aspiration.

entries.source: Bootcamp.com Hematology & Oncology.pdf; Leukemias and Lymphomas - Hairy Cell Leukemia; PDF p. 82

proposal.why: Removes the title-echoing tile; massive splenomegaly is a classic, certain hairy-cell clue (shared with CML/myelofibrosis, which adds discrimination).

entries.auditNote: Hair-like projections echoes the title; BRAF also duplicates a tile in PLX-HEM-050.

revised.title: Hairy-cell-leukemia clues
revised.explanation: Classic hairy cell leukemia carries a BRAF V600E mutation, stains TRAP positive, infiltrates and fibroses the marrow (dry tap), and typically presents with pancytopenia.
revised.detail: Hairy cell leukemia is an indolent mature B-cell neoplasm of middle-aged men. The cells have fine cytoplasmic projections, stain with tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase (largely replaced by flow cytometry for CD11c, CD25, and CD103), and nearly always carry BRAF V600E in the classic form. Marrow infiltration with reticulin fibrosis causes a dry tap and pancytopenia, and splenic infiltration causes massive splenomegaly. Lymphadenopathy is uncommon, and treatment is a purine analogue such as cladribine.
tileNotes: BRAF V600E is present in nearly all cases of classic hairy cell leukemia; the variant form usually lacks it.
The leukemic cells stain positive for tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase, a traditional diagnostic marker.
Marrow infiltration and fibrosis plus splenic sequestration lower all three cell lines; monocytopenia is also typical.
Reticulin fibrosis and packed marrow prevent aspiration, so a core biopsy is needed.

entries.changeSummary: Replaced Hair-like cytoplasmic projections with Pancytopenia rather than the proposed Massive splenomegaly, which duplicates a tile in the myelofibrosis group.
entries.checkNote: Pancytopenia (with monocytopenia) is the classic hairy cell presentation and avoids duplicating massive splenomegaly.

check.note: Pancytopenia (with monocytopenia) is the classic hairy cell presentation and avoids duplicating massive splenomegaly.

original.title: CLL-associated findings
original.explanation: CLL involves a mature clonal lymphocyte population, fragile cells on smear, and risks of immune cytopenias and transformation to aggressive lymphoma.

entries.source: Bootcamp.com Hematology & Oncology.pdf; Leukemias and Lymphomas - CLL; PDF p. 80

proposal.why: Smudge cells is the reflex giveaway; CD5-positive B cells is certain for CLL and forces discrimination from mantle cell lymphoma.

entries.auditNote: Smudge cells and Richter transformation are both CLL giveaways.

revised.title: CLL-associated findings
revised.explanation: CLL is a clonal proliferation of mature CD5-positive B cells that can cause autoimmune cytopenias and transform into an aggressive lymphoma.
revised.detail: CLL is the most common leukemia in older adults in the United States. The neoplastic cells are small, mature-appearing B cells that coexpress CD5 and CD23, producing an absolute lymphocytosis; fragile cells rupture on smear preparation as smudge cells. Immune dysregulation causes hypogammaglobulinemia and autoimmune cytopenias, most often warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia. A minority undergo Richter transformation, usually to diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. Mantle cell lymphoma is also CD5 positive but is CD23 negative and overexpresses cyclin D1 from t(11;14).
tileNotes: CLL cells are B cells that aberrantly express the T-cell marker CD5, along with CD23; mantle cell lymphoma is the main CD5-positive look-alike.
A sustained increase in small, mature-appearing lymphocytes in the blood is the presenting finding in most patients.
Immune dysregulation produces autoantibodies against red cells, usually warm IgG, in a subset of patients.
Transformation of CLL into an aggressive lymphoma, usually diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, with rapid node enlargement and B symptoms.

entries.changeSummary: Replaced Smudge cells with CD5-positive B cells.
entries.checkNote: CD5-positive B cells is the defining CLL immunophenotype clue, and the note names mantle cell lymphoma as the look-alike.

check.note: CD5-positive B cells is the defining CLL immunophenotype clue, and the note names mantle cell lymphoma as the look-alike.

original.title: Monoclonal light-chain disease associations
original.explanation: Monoclonal immunoglobulin light chains can be detected in serum or urine and can injure the kidney or deposit as amyloid.

entries.source: Bootcamp.com Hematology & Oncology.pdf; Plasma Cell Dyscrasias - Multiple Myeloma; PDF p. 87

proposal.why: Abnormal kappa/lambda ratio is the standard way to express an abnormal serum free light-chain assay and removes the title echo.
proposal.changes: Abnormal serum free-light-chain assay -> Abnormal kappa/lambda ratio

entries.auditNote: Requires linking detection findings and complications to monoclonal light chains; free-light-chain repeats the title.

revised.title: Monoclonal light-chain disease associations
revised.explanation: Monoclonal immunoglobulin light chains can be detected in serum or urine and can injure the kidney or deposit as amyloid.
revised.detail: A plasma cell clone that overproduces one light chain type (kappa or lambda) can be detected as Bence Jones protein in urine or as a skewed serum free kappa/lambda ratio. The excess light chains can precipitate in distal tubules with Tamm-Horsfall protein, causing cast nephropathy (myeloma kidney), or misfold and deposit as AL amyloid in organs such as the heart, kidney, and nerves. AL amyloidosis can occur without overt myeloma. AA amyloidosis, by contrast, derives from serum amyloid A in chronic inflammation, not from light chains.
tileNotes: Free monoclonal light chains filtered by the glomerulus and excreted in urine.
Filtered light chains combine with Tamm-Horsfall protein to form obstructing tubular casts, a common cause of renal failure in myeloma.
Misfolded monoclonal light chains deposit as amyloid fibrils, causing restrictive cardiomyopathy, nephrotic syndrome, and neuropathy.
The serum free light chain assay shows a skewed ratio when one clone overproduces a single light chain type.

entries.changeSummary: Replaced Abnormal serum free-light-chain assay with the equivalent Abnormal kappa/lambda ratio; meaning unchanged.
entries.checkNote: cosmetic

check.note: cosmetic

entries.subject: Heme/Onc

original.title: Polycythemia-vera clues
original.explanation: Autonomous myeloid proliferation produces erythrocytosis with suppressed EPO and can cause water-triggered itching and marrow expansion across myeloid lines.

entries.source: Bootcamp.com Hematology & Oncology.pdf; Myeloproliferative Disease - Polycythemia Vera; PDF p. 89

proposal.why: Removes the JAK2 giveaway and cross-group duplicate; erythromelalgia is a certain, characteristic PV (and ET) symptom.

entries.auditNote: JAK2 gives PV away quickly and duplicates the JAK2 tile in PLX-HEM-050.

revised.title: Polycythemia-vera clues
revised.explanation: Autonomous myeloid proliferation in polycythemia vera produces erythrocytosis with suppressed EPO, panmyelosis, and characteristic symptoms such as erythromelalgia and itching after bathing.
revised.detail: Polycythemia vera is a myeloproliferative neoplasm, usually driven by JAK2 V617F, in which marrow precursors proliferate independently of erythropoietin. The red cell mass rises while EPO is suppressed, which separates it from secondary polycythemia (hypoxia or EPO-secreting tumors), where EPO is normal or high. Platelets and granulocytes often increase as well (panmyelosis). Microvascular platelet activity causes erythromelalgia, and mast cell activation contributes to aquagenic pruritus. Thrombosis is the main complication.
tileNotes: Episodic burning pain, redness, and warmth of the hands and feet from platelet-mediated microvascular occlusion; seen in PV and essential thrombocythemia.
Red cell production is autonomous, so feedback suppresses EPO; secondary polycythemia has normal or high EPO.
Itching after a warm bath or shower, thought to reflect histamine release from increased basophils and mast cells.
The marrow is hypercellular across erythroid, granulocytic, and megakaryocytic lines.

entries.changeSummary: Replaced JAK2 mutation with Erythromelalgia to remove the giveaway and the duplicate tile.
entries.checkNote: Erythromelalgia is a textbook PV feature and removes the JAK2 giveaway.

check.note: Erythromelalgia is a textbook PV feature and removes the JAK2 giveaway.

entries.subject: Heme/Onc

original.title: Myelofibrosis clues
original.explanation: Fibrotic marrow and extramedullary hematopoiesis yield teardrop cells, a leukoerythroblastic smear (immature myeloid and nucleated red cells), and marked splenic enlargement.

entries.source: Bootcamp.com Hematology & Oncology.pdf; Myeloproliferative Disease - Myelofibrosis; PDF p. 90

proposal.why: 'Bone marrow fibrosis' is the diagnosis restated; a dry tap is the classic, certain marrow clue and requires a step of reasoning.
proposal.changes: Tile 3 'Bone marrow fibrosis' -> 'Dry tap on aspiration'.

entries.auditNote: Teardrop cells plus 'bone marrow fibrosis' make it quick; the fibrosis tile restates the title.

revised.title: Myelofibrosis clues
revised.explanation: Marrow fibrosis forces blood cell production into the spleen and liver, producing teardrop cells, a leukoerythroblastic smear, and marked splenomegaly.
revised.detail: In primary myelofibrosis, clonal megakaryocytes release fibroblast growth factors and the marrow is progressively replaced by fibrosis. Hematopoiesis shifts to the spleen and liver (extramedullary hematopoiesis), causing massive splenomegaly. Red cells deformed as they leave the fibrotic marrow appear as dacrocytes, and immature granulocytes and nucleated red cells released early create a leukoerythroblastic picture. Marrow aspiration is often a dry tap. Other marrow-infiltrating processes (metastatic cancer, granulomatous disease) can produce a similar smear.
tileNotes: Teardrop-shaped red cells deformed as they squeeze out of the fibrotic marrow.
Circulating immature granulocytes and nucleated red cells, released because the fibrotic marrow cannot retain them.
With the marrow replaced by fibrosis, blood cell production moves to the spleen and liver.
Extramedullary hematopoiesis in the spleen enlarges it markedly, often across the midline.

entries.changeSummary: Replaced Bone marrow fibrosis with Extramedullary hematopoiesis rather than the proposed Dry tap on aspiration, which duplicates the dry tap tile in the hairy cell leukemia group.
entries.checkNote: Extramedullary hematopoiesis is a central myelofibrosis feature and removes the fibrosis restatement without duplicating dry tap.

check.note: Extramedullary hematopoiesis is a central myelofibrosis feature and removes the fibrosis restatement without duplicating dry tap.

entries.subject: Immunology

original.title: Secondary lymphoid tissues
original.explanation: These are sites where mature lymphocytes encounter antigen and mount adaptive responses, rather than the primary sites of lymphocyte development.

entries.source: Bootcamp.com Immunology.pdf; Lymphoid Tissue - primary versus secondary tissues; PDF p. 3

proposal.why: Lymph nodes are the most obvious member; the appendix is certainly gut-associated secondary lymphoid tissue and makes the set less automatic.

entries.auditNote: Spleen and lymph nodes are the textbook secondary lymphoid organs; MALT/appendix also fit.
entries.reason: Drops lymph nodes, the prototypical secondary lymphoid organ, with no giveaway being removed, so the set feels arbitrary. Three of four tiles are now MALT/GALT (appendix, Peyer patches, tonsils), so the set reads like a MALT category with the spleen as the odd one out.

attempted.title: Secondary lymphoid tissues
attempted.explanation: Each is a secondary lymphoid tissue where mature lymphocytes encounter antigen and mount adaptive immune responses.
attempted.detail: Lymphocytes develop in the primary lymphoid organs (bone marrow for B cells, thymus for T cells) and then circulate to secondary lymphoid tissues, where antigen is presented and responses begin. The spleen filters blood-borne antigens and lymph nodes filter lymph. Mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue, including the tonsils, Peyer's patches of the ileum, and the appendix, samples antigens at mucosal surfaces. Bone marrow and thymus are primary, not secondary, lymphoid organs.
tileNotes: Filters blood; the white pulp (periarteriolar lymphoid sheaths and follicles) is where immune responses to blood-borne antigens begin.
Its wall contains abundant lymphoid follicles, making it part of the gut-associated lymphoid tissue.
Lymphoid follicles in the ileal lamina propria and submucosa; M cells overlying them sample intestinal antigens and support IgA production.
Lymphoid tissue of the pharynx (Waldeyer ring) that samples inhaled and ingested antigens.

problems: Drops lymph nodes, the prototypical secondary lymphoid organ, with no giveaway being removed, so the set feels arbitrary.
Three of four tiles are now MALT/GALT (appendix, Peyer patches, tonsils), so the set reads like a MALT category with the spleen as the odd one out.
check.note: Swapping out lymph nodes adds no reasoning value and makes the grouping ambiguous.

entries.subject: Immunology

original.title: Findings of leukocyte adhesion deficiency type 1
original.explanation: Defective CD18-containing beta-2 integrins impair firm adhesion and tissue recruitment of leukocytes, producing this characteristic clinical pattern.

entries.source: Bootcamp.com Immunology.pdf; Inflammation - disorders of leukocyte migration; PDF p. 18

proposal.why: Tile 4 restates the disease name; marked neutrophilia (neutrophils cannot leave vessels) is a certain, classic LAD-1 finding that requires mechanistic thought.

entries.auditNote: Delayed cord separation is a classic instant clue, and 'leukocyte adhesion' in tile 4 repeats the title.

revised.title: Findings of leukocyte adhesion deficiency type 1
revised.explanation: Defective CD18 beta-2 integrins stop neutrophils from adhering firmly and leaving vessels, so they pile up in the blood but fail to reach tissues.
revised.detail: LAD type 1 is an autosomal recessive defect in CD18, the shared subunit of the beta-2 integrins such as LFA-1. Without it, neutrophils roll but cannot adhere firmly to endothelium or migrate into tissue. Neutrophils therefore accumulate in the blood (marked neutrophilia even without infection), while infected sites lack pus, wounds heal poorly, and the umbilical cord separates late (after about 30 days). Chronic granulomatous disease differs: neutrophils reach tissue but cannot kill catalase-positive organisms.
tileNotes: Neutrophils are needed to separate the cord stump; separation after about 30 days is a classic early clue.
Neutrophils cannot leave vessels, so bacterial infections occur without pus formation.
Impaired neutrophil recruitment slows the inflammatory phase of repair, so wounds heal poorly.
Neutrophils cannot exit the circulation, so blood neutrophil counts are high even without active infection.

entries.changeSummary: Replaced Defective firm leukocyte adhesion, which restated the disease name, with Marked neutrophilia.
entries.checkNote: Marked neutrophilia is a classic LAD1 finding and replaces the tile that restated the mechanism.

check.note: Marked neutrophilia is a classic LAD1 finding and replaces the tile that restated the mechanism.

proposal.title: MHC class I features
proposal.why: Removes the title word 'presentation' that also appears in tile 3; membership unchanged.

revised.title: MHC class I features
revised.explanation: MHC class I molecules contain beta-2 microglobulin, are expressed on most nucleated cells, and usually present intracellularly derived peptides to CD8 T cells.
revised.detail: MHC class I (HLA-A, -B, -C) consists of a heavy chain paired with beta-2 microglobulin. Cytosolic proteins are degraded by the proteasome and transported into the endoplasmic reticulum by TAP, where peptides load onto class I. Nearly all nucleated cells express class I, letting CD8 cytotoxic T cells detect viral infection or malignancy. Red blood cells lack it. MHC class II, by contrast, is restricted to antigen-presenting cells and presents exogenous peptides to CD4 T cells; cross-presentation by dendritic cells is the main exception to the endogenous rule.
tileNotes: CD8 on cytotoxic T cells binds the alpha-3 domain of MHC class I, restricting these cells to class I-presented antigen.
The invariant light chain that pairs with the class I heavy chain; it is not encoded in the MHC.
Cytosolic proteins are cleaved by the proteasome and loaded via TAP in the endoplasmic reticulum, so class I usually shows endogenous peptides.
Class I is present on virtually all nucleated cells (not red blood cells), allowing CD8 T cells to survey most tissues.

revised.title: MHC class II features
revised.explanation: MHC class II molecules, encoded by HLA-DP, DQ and DR, use the invariant chain during assembly and typically present endocytosed antigen to CD4 T cells.
revised.detail: MHC class II is expressed mainly on professional antigen-presenting cells (dendritic cells, macrophages, B cells). In the endoplasmic reticulum the invariant chain occupies the peptide-binding groove and directs the molecule to endosomes, where it is degraded and replaced by peptides from internalized proteins. The loaded molecule then presents these exogenous peptides to CD4 helper T cells. MHC class I differs by using beta-2 microglobulin, presenting cytosolic peptides, and engaging CD8 T cells; autophagy can occasionally deliver endogenous peptides to class II.

The three HLA loci that encode MHC class II molecules (class I is HLA-A, -B, -C).

revised.title: Clues to X-linked agammaglobulinemia
revised.explanation: BTK-related failure of B-cell maturation produces very few mature B cells, deficient antibody production, small or absent lymphoid tissue, and susceptibility to enteroviruses.
revised.detail: X-linked (Bruton) agammaglobulinemia is caused by BTK mutations that arrest B-cell development at the pre-B stage. Boys present after about 6 months, when maternal IgG wanes, with recurrent bacterial sinopulmonary infections from encapsulated organisms. Circulating B cells are nearly absent and all immunoglobulin classes are very low, so tonsils and lymph nodes are small or absent. Because antibody is the main defense against enteroviruses, patients can develop chronic enteroviral meningoencephalitis and vaccine-associated polio, so live vaccines are avoided. Common variable immunodeficiency differs by presenting later, with B cells present.
tileNotes: Antibody is needed to clear enteroviruses, so patients can develop persistent echovirus or coxsackievirus infection of the brain and meninges.
BTK deficiency blocks maturation at the pre-B stage, so circulating CD19-positive B cells are nearly absent.
Without mature B cells and plasma cells, all immunoglobulin classes are very low.
Lymphoid tissues lack B-cell follicles and germinal centers, so tonsils and lymph nodes are small or absent.

tiles: Low IgA with preserved IgG / IgM
revised.explanation: Selective IgA deficiency can weaken mucosal defense, interfere with IgA-based celiac testing, and in a small subset be associated with anaphylactic transfusion reactions from anti-IgA antibodies.
revised.detail: Selective IgA deficiency is the most common primary immunodeficiency, defined by very low serum IgA with normal IgG and IgM. Many patients are asymptomatic, but some have sinopulmonary and gastrointestinal infections such as giardiasis, along with higher rates of autoimmune disease and celiac disease. Because tTG-IgA will be falsely negative, celiac screening should use IgG-based tests. Some patients form anti-IgA antibodies and can have anaphylaxis when transfused with products containing IgA; this is uncommon, and washed or IgA-deficient products are used when it is a concern.

Reduced secretory IgA weakens mucosal defense, predisposing to chronic Giardia infection with diarrhea.
Patients cannot make IgA antibodies, so IgA-based celiac serology is falsely negative and IgG-based testing is needed.

revised.title: CD40L-deficient hyper-IgM clues
revised.explanation: Deficient T-cell CD40 ligand impairs class switching and T-cell help to macrophages, leaving IgM preserved or high, switched isotypes low, and susceptibility to opportunistic infections such as Pneumocystis.
revised.detail: In the X-linked form of hyper-IgM syndrome, activated helper T cells lack CD40 ligand, so they cannot signal B cells through CD40 to undergo class switch recombination. IgM is normal or elevated while IgG, IgA and IgE are low, causing recurrent pyogenic infections. CD40L is also needed for T-cell activation of macrophages, so patients get opportunistic infections such as Pneumocystis pneumonia and Cryptosporidium. AID deficiency also causes hyper-IgM but is a B-cell intrinsic defect without opportunistic infections.
tileNotes: Loss of CD40L-mediated T-cell help to macrophages causes opportunistic infection, and Pneumocystis pneumonia in infancy is a classic presentation.
B cells do not receive the CD40 signal needed for class switch recombination.
B cells can still make IgM, which is normal or elevated because they cannot switch away from it.
Class-switched isotypes are deficient, causing recurrent sinopulmonary and other pyogenic infections.

DOCK8 deficiency also causes high IgE and eczema but is autosomal recessive with severe viral skin infections and lacks the dental and skeletal features.

revised.explanation: WAS protein dysfunction produces an immunodeficiency with a characteristic immunoglobulin pattern, eczema, and thrombocytopenia with small platelets.
revised.detail: Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome is an X-linked defect in WAS protein, which links surface signals to the actin cytoskeleton in leukocytes and platelets. The classic triad is thrombocytopenia with small platelets, eczema, and recurrent infections, especially with encapsulated organisms because responses to polysaccharide antigens are poor. Immunoglobulins typically show low IgM, normal IgG, and elevated IgA and IgE. Patients are also at risk for autoimmune disease and lymphoma. Immune thrombocytopenia differs by having normal or large platelets.

Eczema and recurrent infections are two parts of the classic triad.
Low platelet counts cause petechiae and bleeding, often the first sign in infancy.

revised.title: Classic type III hypersensitivity examples
revised.explanation: In each example, antigen-antibody complexes deposit in tissue, fix complement, and drive inflammation (type III hypersensitivity).
revised.detail: Type III hypersensitivity occurs when circulating or locally formed immune complexes deposit in vessel walls or tissues, activate complement, and attract neutrophils. Serum sickness is systemic (fever, rash, arthralgia, proteinuria about 1 to 2 weeks after exposure to foreign protein or certain drugs), while the Arthus reaction is localized skin necrosis at an injection site. Poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis and lupus nephritis are immune-complex kidney diseases with low complement. Type II reactions differ because antibody binds antigen fixed on cells or tissue rather than forming soluble complexes.

revised.title: Hyperacute graft rejection clues
revised.explanation: Hyperacute rejection is caused by preformed recipient antibodies against donor antigens, producing vascular thrombosis and necrosis within minutes of reperfusion.
revised.detail: Preformed antibodies (classically ABO or anti-HLA from prior transfusion, pregnancy, or transplant) bind donor endothelium as soon as blood flows through the graft. Complement activation and endothelial injury cause thrombosis of small vessels, fibrinoid necrosis of vessel walls, and ischemic graft loss. This is a type II hypersensitivity reaction and is distinct from acute rejection (days to weeks, mostly T-cell mediated) and chronic rejection (months to years, vascular narrowing and fibrosis). Pretransplant crossmatching is designed to prevent it.
tileNotes: Preformed recipient antibodies against donor ABO or HLA antigens are the cause of hyperacute rejection; they exist before the transplant.
Because the antibodies are already present, damage begins within minutes of restoring blood flow to the graft, often visible in the operating room.
Antibody and complement binding to graft endothelium triggers platelet aggregation and thrombosis of small vessels, leading to ischemia.
Vessel walls in the graft show fibrinoid necrosis from antibody-mediated endothelial and vascular injury.

revised.title: Anti-TNF biologics
revised.explanation: Each is a biologic that neutralizes tumor necrosis factor alpha.
revised.detail: Infliximab (chimeric) and adalimumab (fully human) are monoclonal antibodies against TNF-alpha, certolizumab is a PEGylated Fab' fragment, and etanercept is a fusion protein of the TNF receptor and IgG1 Fc that acts as a decoy receptor. All are used in conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, and ankylosing spondylitis, and all carry a risk of serious infection including reactivation of latent tuberculosis. They differ from biologics that target other cytokines or cells, such as tocilizumab (IL-6 receptor), anakinra (IL-1), abatacept (T-cell costimulation), and rituximab (CD20).
tileNotes: Infliximab is a chimeric monoclonal antibody that binds TNF-alpha; it is given intravenously.
Adalimumab is a fully human monoclonal antibody that binds TNF-alpha; it is given subcutaneously.
Etanercept is a recombinant TNF receptor fused to IgG1 Fc that binds and neutralizes TNF as a decoy receptor; it is not a monoclonal antibody.
Certolizumab pegol is a PEGylated Fab' fragment that binds TNF-alpha; it lacks an Fc region.

revised.title: Diagnostic clues for Legionnaires disease
revised.explanation: Each is a classic clue to Legionella pneumophila pneumonia: its environmental source, typical clinical and laboratory features, and its culture medium.
revised.detail: Legionella lives in water systems (cooling towers, hot tubs, plumbing) and is acquired by inhaling aerosols, not by person-to-person spread. Legionnaires disease is an atypical pneumonia that often has extrapulmonary features such as diarrhea, confusion, and hyponatremia. The organism stains poorly on Gram stain and needs buffered charcoal yeast extract agar with iron and cysteine to grow. Urine antigen testing is also used but mainly detects serogroup 1. These features help separate it from Mycoplasma and Chlamydophila, the other common atypical pneumonias.
tileNotes: Legionella grows in water systems such as cooling towers and hot tubs, and infection follows inhalation of contaminated aerosols.
Hyponatremia is a classic laboratory clue in Legionella pneumonia, more frequent than in most other community-acquired pneumonias.
Gastrointestinal symptoms, especially diarrhea, accompanying pneumonia are a classic clue to Legionnaires disease.
Legionella requires buffered charcoal yeast extract (BCYE) agar, supplemented with iron and cysteine, for culture.

revised.title: Late congenital-syphilis stigmata
revised.explanation: Each is a late manifestation of congenital syphilis, appearing after age 2 years.
revised.detail: Late congenital syphilis reflects chronic Treponema pallidum inflammation of developing bone, cartilage, cornea, and the eighth cranial nerve. Classic stigmata include interstitial keratitis, eighth-nerve deafness, saber shins (anterior tibial bowing), saddle nose, Hutchinson teeth, and mulberry molars. Early congenital syphilis (before age 2) instead features rhinitis (snuffles), rash, hepatosplenomegaly, and osteochondritis. Each tile has look-alike causes (Cogan syndrome for keratitis with deafness, granulomatosis with polyangiitis for saddle nose), so the shared link must be recognized as a set.
tileNotes: Interstitial keratitis (corneal stromal inflammation) typically appears between ages 5 and 20 in congenital syphilis and is part of the Hutchinson triad.
Saber shins are anterior bowing of the tibia from chronic periostitis, a late skeletal stigma of congenital syphilis.
Saddle nose results from destruction of nasal cartilage and bone, a late facial stigma of congenital syphilis.
Eighth cranial nerve involvement causes sensorineural deafness, usually appearing in late childhood, and is part of the Hutchinson triad.

original.explanation: Cryptococcus has a prominent polysaccharide capsule demonstrable by these stains or by antigen assay (which detects capsular polysaccharide, glucuronoxylomannan); CNS infection can produce gelatinous pseudocysts. Imaging findings are neither required nor exclusive.

proposal.why: Removes the tile that names the organism; markedly elevated CSF opening pressure is a definite, clinically important feature of cryptococcal meningitis.
proposal.changes: Replace 'Positive cryptococcal antigen' with 'High CSF opening pressure'.

entries.auditNote: 'Cryptococcal antigen' names the organism, and India ink/mucicarmine are instant buzzwords.
entries.reason: High CSF opening pressure is not a Cryptococcus diagnostic feature in the sense of the title; it is nonspecific and a classic tile for idiopathic intracranial hypertension and bacterial meningitis CSF lists, so it creates unfair board ambiguity.

attempted.title: Cryptococcus diagnostic features
attempted.explanation: Each is a characteristic finding in cryptococcal infection, reflecting its polysaccharide capsule or the meningoencephalitis it causes.
attempted.detail: Cryptococcus neoformans is an encapsulated yeast whose thick polysaccharide capsule appears as a clear halo on India ink preparation and stains red with mucicarmine. Cryptococcal meningitis, especially in HIV, often causes markedly raised CSF opening pressure, which needs repeated lumbar drainage. Gelatinous capsular material can collect in perivascular spaces and the basal ganglia, producing soap-bubble pseudocysts. Antigen testing for capsular polysaccharide is the most sensitive diagnostic test.
tileNotes: India ink outlines the unstained polysaccharide capsule of Cryptococcus as a clear halo around the yeast in CSF.
Mucicarmine stains the polysaccharide capsule of Cryptococcus red in tissue sections, distinguishing it from other yeasts.
Cryptococcal meningitis frequently causes markedly elevated CSF opening pressure, a finding that guides management with therapeutic lumbar punctures.
Gelatinous capsular material in dilated perivascular spaces produces soap-bubble pseudocysts, classically in the basal ganglia.

problems: High CSF opening pressure is not a Cryptococcus diagnostic feature in the sense of the title; it is nonspecific and a classic tile for idiopathic intracranial hypertension and bacterial meningitis CSF lists, so it creates unfair board ambiguity.
check.note: Replacement tile is nonspecific and fits other classic lists better than a Cryptococcus diagnostic set.

entries.subject: Microbiology

original.title: Invasive pulmonary aspergillosis clues
original.explanation: Invasive Aspergillus infection can yield septate acute-angle branching hyphae, galactomannan positivity, pulmonary nodules/cavitation, and bleeding from tissue/vascular invasion. No single clue is fully specific.

entries.source: Bootcamp.com Microbiology.pdf; Aspergillus (p. 125); Opportunistic Infections (p. 273)

proposal.why: The halo sign (nodule with surrounding ground-glass) is a definite classic imaging clue of angioinvasive pulmonary aspergillosis and is less of a buzzword than the hyphae description.
proposal.changes: Replace 'Septate acute-angle branching hyphae' with 'CT halo sign'.

entries.auditNote: Septate acute-angle hyphae is the textbook Aspergillus descriptor and gives the group away.

revised.title: Invasive pulmonary aspergillosis clues
revised.explanation: Each is a classic clue to angioinvasive Aspergillus infection of the lung, usually in a neutropenic or otherwise immunocompromised patient.
revised.detail: Aspergillus hyphae invade blood vessels, causing hemorrhagic infarction of lung tissue. On CT this produces nodules with a surrounding ground-glass halo of hemorrhage, which later cavitate (air-crescent sign) as neutrophils recover. Galactomannan, a cell-wall antigen, is detected in serum or BAL fluid. Vascular invasion can cause hemoptysis. These features differ from allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (asthma, eosinophilia) and aspergilloma (fungus ball in a preexisting cavity).
tileNotes: The halo sign is a nodule surrounded by ground-glass opacity from hemorrhage, a classic early CT finding of angioinvasive aspergillosis in neutropenic patients.
Galactomannan is an Aspergillus cell-wall polysaccharide detected in serum or bronchoalveolar lavage fluid, supporting the diagnosis.
Aspergillus invades pulmonary vessels and causes hemorrhagic infarction, which can present as hemoptysis in immunocompromised patients.
Angioinvasion produces infarcted nodules that can cavitate, often with an air-crescent sign during neutrophil recovery.

entries.changeSummary: Replaced 'Septate acute-angle branching hyphae' with 'CT halo sign'.
entries.checkNote: CT halo sign is a classic angioinvasive aspergillosis clue; content accurate.

check.note: CT halo sign is a classic angioinvasive aspergillosis clue; content accurate.

entries.subject: Microbiology

original.title: Parasites acquired through infected meat or fish larvae
original.explanation: Ingestion of larvae in infected pork, beef, game meat, or freshwater fish causes intestinal taeniasis, trichinellosis, or fish-tapeworm infection. T. solium EGG ingestion (not pork cysticerci) causes cysticercosis.

entries.source: Bootcamp.com Microbiology.pdf; Taenia (p. 164); Trichinella (p. 157); Diphyllobothriid (p. 165)

proposal.why: Removes the paired Taenia giveaway; Anisakis is definitively acquired by eating raw fish containing larvae and is a common expected member.

entries.auditNote: Two Taenia tiles pair up instantly; Anisakis (fish larvae) and Clonorchis (fish metacercariae) also fit.

revised.title: Parasites acquired by eating larvae in meat or fish
revised.explanation: Each parasite infects humans when larvae in undercooked meat or raw fish are eaten.
revised.detail: Taenia solium cysticerci in undercooked pork develop into adult intestinal tapeworms (taeniasis). Trichinella larvae encysted in pork or game meat cause trichinellosis. Dibothriocephalus latus (formerly Diphyllobothrium latum) plerocercoid larvae in freshwater fish cause fish tapeworm infection and vitamin B12 deficiency. Anisakis larvae in raw marine fish (such as sushi) invade the gastric or intestinal wall. In contrast, cysticercosis results from swallowing T. solium eggs, not from eating larvae in meat.
tileNotes: Eating undercooked pork containing Taenia solium cysticerci (larvae) causes intestinal taeniasis; cysticercosis instead follows ingestion of eggs.
Anisakis larvae in raw or undercooked marine fish are swallowed and invade the stomach or intestinal wall, causing anisakiasis.
Trichinella spiralis larvae encysted in muscle of undercooked pork or game meat cause trichinellosis when eaten.
Dibothriocephalus latus (fish tapeworm) is acquired by eating plerocercoid larvae in raw freshwater fish and can cause vitamin B12 deficiency.

entries.changeSummary: Replaced 'Taenia saginata' with 'Anisakis simplex' to break the paired Taenia tiles, and reworded the title for clarity.
entries.checkNote: Anisakis larvae in raw marine fish fit the title; explanation and notes accurate.

check.note: Anisakis larvae in raw marine fish fit the title; explanation and notes accurate.

entries.subject: Microbiology

original.title: Hydatid disease diagnostic and complication clues
original.explanation: Echinococcus granulosus cycles between canine definitive hosts and intermediate hosts such as sheep. Humans ingest eggs and may develop hepatic cysts; rupture can provoke severe allergic reactions. Calcification is possible, not universal.

entries.source: Bootcamp.com Microbiology.pdf; Echinococcus (p. 166)

proposal.why: Removes the title word; daughter cysts within a hepatic cyst are a definite characteristic finding of cystic echinococcosis.
proposal.changes: Replace 'Hepatic hydatid cyst' with 'Liver cyst with daughter cysts'.

entries.auditNote: 'Hepatic hydatid cyst' repeats the title and dog-sheep cycle is an instant giveaway.

revised.title: Hydatid disease diagnostic and complication clues
revised.explanation: Each is a classic feature of cystic echinococcosis caused by Echinococcus granulosus.
revised.detail: Dogs are the definitive host and sheep the usual intermediate host; humans are accidental intermediate hosts infected by swallowing eggs in dog feces. Larvae most often form cysts in the liver, which can contain daughter cysts and develop eggshell (rim) calcification. Cyst rupture or leakage, including during aspiration, can release antigenic fluid and cause anaphylaxis. This differs from Echinococcus multilocularis (alveolar disease, fox reservoir), which grows infiltratively like a tumor.
tileNotes: Echinococcus granulosus cycles between dogs (definitive host) and sheep (intermediate host); humans are infected by swallowing eggs from dog feces.
The liver is the most common site of hydatid cysts, which classically contain internal daughter cysts on imaging.
Hydatid cyst walls can calcify in a thin peripheral rim, giving an eggshell appearance on imaging.
Rupture or leakage of hydatid cyst fluid, which is highly antigenic, can cause anaphylaxis; this is why careless aspiration is avoided.

entries.changeSummary: Replaced 'Hepatic hydatid cyst' (which repeated the title word) with 'Liver cyst with daughter cysts'.
entries.checkNote: Daughter cysts are a classic hydatid imaging clue and remove the title-word echo.

check.note: Daughter cysts are a classic hydatid imaging clue and remove the title-word echo.

entries.subject: Microbiology

original.title: Segmented RNA virus groups
original.explanation: These groups have segmented RNA genomes that permit reassortment. Rotavirus has 11 double-stranded RNA segments; influenza A/B have 8; arenaviruses have 2 (ambisense); traditional bunyavirus groups have 3 negative-sense/ambisense segments.

entries.source: Bootcamp.com Microbiology.pdf; Viral Genetics (p. 185); Arenavirus (p. 213); Bunyavirus (p. 214); Rotavirus (p. 229)

proposal.why: The parenthetical taxonomy note makes the tile long and odd-looking; 'Bunyavirales' alone is the current standard name with the same meaning.

entries.auditNote: BOAR mnemonic makes this instant; the Bunyavirales tile is wordy and its parenthetical is distracting.
entries.reason: Shortening the Bunyavirales tile is a wording cleanup that does not change the reasoning or remove the BOAR giveaway (cosmetic).

entries.subject: Microbiology

original.title: EBV-associated malignant conditions
original.explanation: EBV is strongly linked to endemic Burkitt lymphoma and AIDS-associated primary CNS lymphoma and to subsets of Hodgkin lymphoma and nasopharyngeal carcinoma. Qualifiers prevent treating all tumors in these classes as EBV-caused.

entries.source: Bootcamp.com Microbiology.pdf; Epstein-Barr Virus (p. 243); Opportunistic Infections (p. 273)

proposal.why: Removes the tile that names the virus; PTLD is a definite, classic EBV-driven malignancy in immunosuppressed transplant recipients.
proposal.changes: Replace 'EBV-positive Hodgkin lymphoma' with 'Post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder'.

entries.auditNote: 'EBV-positive' in a tile names the link outright.

revised.title: EBV-associated malignant conditions
revised.explanation: Each is a neoplastic condition strongly associated with Epstein-Barr virus infection.
revised.detail: EBV infects B cells and certain epithelial cells and can drive their proliferation, particularly when T-cell control is lost. Endemic (African) Burkitt lymphoma, nonkeratinizing nasopharyngeal carcinoma, AIDS-associated primary CNS lymphoma, and most early post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorders are EBV-associated. Not every case in these categories is EBV-positive (for example, some late-onset PTLD), so the link is association rather than universal causation. Other oncogenic viruses differ: HHV-8 with Kaposi sarcoma, HTLV-1 with adult T-cell leukemia, HPV with cervical and oropharyngeal cancer.
tileNotes: Nearly all endemic (African) Burkitt lymphoma is EBV-positive, in contrast to the sporadic form, where the association is weaker.
PTLD is a spectrum of lymphoid proliferations, up to frank lymphoma, after transplantation; most early cases are driven by EBV-infected B cells escaping T-cell control under immunosuppression.
Nasopharyngeal carcinoma, especially the nonkeratinizing type common in southern China and North Africa, is strongly associated with EBV.
Primary CNS lymphoma in patients with AIDS is almost always EBV-positive, a feature used in diagnosis.

entries.changeSummary: Replaced 'EBV-positive Hodgkin lymphoma' (which named the virus) with 'Post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder'.
entries.checkNote: PTLD is a standard EBV-associated malignancy and removes the virus name from the tile.

check.note: PTLD is a standard EBV-associated malignancy and removes the virus name from the tile.

entries.subject: Microbiology

original.title: Congenital rubella manifestations
original.explanation: Congenital rubella has a classic cardiac-ocular-auditory triad (PDA, cataracts, deafness), with dermal extramedullary hematopoiesis sometimes producing a blueberry-muffin rash. The rash is not rubella-specific.

entries.source: Bootcamp.com Microbiology.pdf; Rubella Virus, Congenital Rubella Syndrome (p. 203)

proposal.why: Breaking the memorized triad forces recall; salt-and-pepper retinopathy is a definite classic congenital rubella finding.

entries.auditNote: PDA, cataracts and deafness form the classic congenital rubella triad, so the group is instant.

revised.title: Congenital rubella manifestations
revised.explanation: Each is a classic finding in congenital rubella syndrome after maternal infection in early pregnancy.
revised.detail: Rubella infection in the first trimester disrupts organogenesis, classically causing cardiac defects (PDA, pulmonary artery stenosis), eye disease (cataracts, salt-and-pepper retinopathy, glaucoma), and sensorineural deafness. Dermal extramedullary hematopoiesis can produce a blueberry-muffin rash. Deafness and blueberry-muffin rash also occur with congenital CMV, but CMV is more associated with periventricular calcifications and chorioretinitis; PDA and the pigmentary retinopathy point to rubella.
tileNotes: PDA is the most typical cardiac defect in congenital rubella syndrome.
A pigmentary salt-and-pepper retinopathy is one of the most common eye findings in congenital rubella and usually spares vision.
Sensorineural hearing loss is the most common single manifestation of congenital rubella.
Dermal extramedullary hematopoiesis in congenital rubella causes purple papules called a blueberry-muffin rash; congenital CMV can cause the same rash.

entries.changeSummary: Replaced 'Cataracts' with 'Salt-and-pepper retinopathy' so the tiles no longer form the memorized triad.
entries.checkNote: Salt-and-pepper retinopathy is a classic congenital rubella finding; notes accurate.

check.note: Salt-and-pepper retinopathy is a classic congenital rubella finding; notes accurate.

entries.subject: Microbiology

original.title: Parvovirus B19 clinical syndromes
original.explanation: B19 can cause childhood exanthem and adult arthropathy; suppression of erythroid precursors causes aplastic crisis in high-turnover states and fetal anemia with hydrops after transplacental infection.

entries.source: Bootcamp.com Microbiology.pdf; Parvovirus B19 (p. 232)

proposal.why: Erythema infectiosum is the instant giveaway; papular-purpuric gloves-and-socks syndrome is a definite, well-described parvovirus B19 syndrome.

entries.auditNote: Erythema infectiosum names parvovirus B19 outright; other tiles follow instantly.
entries.reason: Papular-purpuric gloves-and-socks syndrome is beyond standard student-level knowledge and makes a long tile.

entries.subject: Microbiology

original.title: Classic peripheral endocarditis findings
original.explanation: Classic peripheral findings that can accompany infective endocarditis through vascular/embolic or immune-mediated phenomena. Their absence does not exclude endocarditis, and none is fully specific.

entries.source: Bootcamp.com Microbiology.pdf; Endocarditis (p. 255)

proposal.why: Janeway lesions are the most endocarditis-specific giveaway; conjunctival petechiae are a definite classic peripheral sign of infective endocarditis, and the remaining tiles keep decoys (leukemia, trauma).

entries.auditNote: Janeway/Osler/Roth/splinter is the memorized endocarditis set; conjunctival petechiae is an equally classic member.

revised.title: Classic peripheral endocarditis findings
revised.explanation: Each is a classic extracardiac sign of infective endocarditis, caused by emboli, vascular injury, or immune complex deposition.
revised.detail: Infective endocarditis produces peripheral signs from septic microemboli and vasculitis. Conjunctival petechiae and splinter hemorrhages reflect small-vessel injury or emboli, while Osler nodes (painful finger-pad nodules) and Roth spots (retinal hemorrhages with pale centers) are classically attributed to immune complexes. Janeway lesions (painless palm and sole macules) belong to the same set. None of these signs is fully specific: splinter hemorrhages follow trauma, and Roth spots and petechiae occur in leukemia and severe anemia.
tileNotes: Petechiae on the palpebral conjunctiva are a classic peripheral sign of infective endocarditis from small-vessel emboli or vascular injury.
Osler nodes are painful, tender nodules on finger or toe pads, classically attributed to immune complex deposition in endocarditis.
Roth spots are retinal hemorrhages with pale centers seen in infective endocarditis, though also found in leukemia and anemia.
Splinter hemorrhages are linear dark red streaks under the nails from microemboli or vascular injury; trauma is a common nonendocarditis cause.

entries.changeSummary: Replaced 'Janeway lesions' with 'Conjunctival petechiae' to break the memorized Janeway, Osler, Roth, splinter set.
entries.checkNote: Conjunctival petechiae are a standard peripheral endocarditis sign; content accurate.

check.note: Conjunctival petechiae are a standard peripheral endocarditis sign; content accurate.

entries.subject: Microbiology

original.title: Antibiotic groups acting on the 50S ribosome
original.explanation: These agents/classes inhibit bacterial translation at the 50S subunit, with differing effects on translocation, initiation, or peptidyl transfer. The shared subunit does not mean an identical binding site.

entries.source: Bootcamp.com Microbiology.pdf; Antibiotics Overview (p. 277); 50S Ribosomal Inhibitors (p. 284)

proposal.why: Replaces the drug-class tile with a single macrolide so all four tiles are the same kind of item; erythromycin certainly binds the 50S subunit.

entries.auditNote: Mnemonic-driven 50S list; one class tile among single drugs is a format tell, and streptogramins also fit.
entries.reason: Swapping the class 'Macrolides' for 'Erythromycin' leaves an equally recognizable 50S list and adds no reasoning (cosmetic).

entries.subject: MSK

original.title: Medications that can promote hyperuricemia
original.explanation: These agents can raise serum urate and contribute to gout risk. The aspirin effect is dose-dependent: low-dose (<=2 g/day) raises urate while high-dose (>3 g/day) is uricosuric, so the tile specifies low-dose aspirin.

entries.source: Bootcamp.com MSK.pdf; Non-Rheumatologic Diseases / Gout; PDF pp. 11

proposal.why: Two 'diuretics' tiles pair off on wording; pyrazinamide certainly raises serum urate (inhibits renal urate excretion) and is the member players most expect.

entries.auditNote: Classic hyperuricemia list; two diuretic tiles share a stem, and pyrazinamide, a staple of the same list, is a likely expected member.

revised.title: Medications that can promote hyperuricemia
revised.explanation: Each drug raises serum urate, mainly by reducing renal urate excretion, and can precipitate gout.
revised.detail: Thiazides cause volume contraction and compete with urate for tubular secretion, increasing proximal reabsorption. Pyrazinamide's metabolite pyrazinoic acid stimulates urate reabsorption via URAT1. Low-dose salicylate reduces urate excretion, while high doses are uricosuric. Niacin competes for renal urate excretion. Other drugs with this effect include loop diuretics, ethambutol, and cyclosporine; contrast drugs that lower urate, such as probenecid, losartan, and allopurinol.
tileNotes: Thiazides raise serum urate through volume contraction and competition with urate for proximal tubular secretion.
Pyrazinamide's metabolite pyrazinoic acid promotes renal urate reabsorption, so hyperuricemia is common during tuberculosis treatment.
Low-dose aspirin reduces renal urate excretion and raises serum urate; high doses have the opposite, uricosuric effect.
Niacin (nicotinic acid) reduces renal urate excretion and can precipitate gout attacks.

entries.changeSummary: Replaced 'Loop diuretics' with 'Pyrazinamide' so two diuretic tiles no longer pair off.
entries.checkNote: Pyrazinamide is a classic urate-raising drug and removes the paired diuretics.

check.note: Pyrazinamide is a classic urate-raising drug and removes the paired diuretics.

entries.subject: MSK

original.title: CPP crystal arthritis diagnostic clues
tiles: Blue when aligned parallel to the compensator
original.explanation: CPP crystals are typically rhomboid and weakly positively birefringent; under a compensator they appear blue when aligned parallel to its slow axis. Cartilage calcification (chondrocalcinosis) supports CPPD but can be absent and is not specific.

entries.source: Bootcamp.com MSK.pdf; Non-Rheumatologic Diseases / CPPD; PDF pp. 12

proposal.title: CPP crystal deposition disease clues
proposal.why: Removes the redundant optical descriptor and adds a classic, certain CPPD association that requires recall rather than repeating crystal optics.
proposal.changes: Replace 'Blue when aligned parallel to the compensator' with 'Hemochromatosis'; title broadened from arthritis to deposition disease so an associated condition fits.

entries.auditNote: Tiles 2 and 4 describe the same optical property (blue parallel is how weak positive birefringence appears), so the group is padded with a duplicate.
entries.reason: Hemochromatosis is a disease association, not a diagnostic clue of CPP crystal disease; mixing it with crystal and imaging findings makes the title stretch, and it fits many other classic lists (HLA-A3, secondary diabetes, cardiomyopathy causes). Rhomboid crystals and weak positive birefringence remain paired crystal descriptors, so the overlap concern is only partly addressed.

attempted.title: CPP crystal deposition disease clues
attempted.explanation: Each is a classic diagnostic feature of, or condition associated with, calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease (pseudogout).
attempted.detail: CPP crystals in synovial fluid are rhomboid and weakly positively birefringent (blue when parallel to the compensator axis). Chondrocalcinosis, calcification of cartilage such as the knee menisci or wrist triangular fibrocartilage, is the radiographic hallmark. CPPD is associated with metabolic diseases including hemochromatosis, hyperparathyroidism, hypomagnesemia, and hypophosphatasia, and these should be sought in younger patients. Gout differs: urate crystals are needle-shaped and strongly negatively birefringent.
tileNotes: CPP crystals are typically rhomboid or rod-shaped, in contrast to the needle-shaped monosodium urate crystals of gout.
CPP crystals show weak positive birefringence under polarized light, appearing blue when parallel to the compensator axis.
Chondrocalcinosis is calcification of articular cartilage seen on radiographs and is the imaging hallmark of CPPD.
Hemochromatosis is a classic metabolic association of CPPD; iron deposition promotes CPP crystal formation, often with second and third MCP joint involvement.

problems: Hemochromatosis is a disease association, not a diagnostic clue of CPP crystal disease; mixing it with crystal and imaging findings makes the title stretch, and it fits many other classic lists (HLA-A3, secondary diabetes, cardiomyopathy causes).
Rhomboid crystals and weak positive birefringence remain paired crystal descriptors, so the overlap concern is only partly addressed.
check.note: Hemochromatosis is an associated condition that fits other classic lists better than a CPPD clues set.

entries.subject: MSK

original.title: Medications classically linked to drug-induced lupus
original.explanation: These drugs can cause a lupus-like syndrome; risk is highest with procainamide and hydralazine. Anti-histone antibodies are typical but not uniquely diagnostic.

entries.source: Bootcamp.com MSK.pdf; Rheumatologic Diseases / SLE, Drug-induced lupus; PDF pp. 28

proposal.why: Procainamide is the single most cued drug-induced lupus agent; minocycline is a well-established, certain cause that requires genuine recall and tempts toward other categories (tetracyclines, hyperpigmentation).

entries.auditNote: Hydralazine plus procainamide (SHIPP/HIPP mnemonic) gives the group away at once.

revised.title: Medications classically linked to drug-induced lupus
revised.explanation: Each drug can cause a reversible lupus-like syndrome that resolves after the drug is stopped.
revised.detail: Drug-induced lupus typically presents with arthralgia, fever, and serositis, with antinuclear and often anti-histone antibodies; renal and CNS disease are uncommon, and anti-dsDNA is usually absent. Classic culprits include hydralazine, procainamide, isoniazid, methyldopa, minocycline, quinidine, and anti-TNF agents. Many of these drugs are slow-acetylator substrates (hydralazine, procainamide, isoniazid). Minocycline-induced lupus often has positive p-ANCA rather than anti-histone antibodies.
tileNotes: Hydralazine is one of the highest-risk causes of drug-induced lupus, especially in slow acetylators.
Minocycline, a tetracycline used long-term for acne, is a well-established cause of drug-induced lupus, often with p-ANCA positivity.
Isoniazid can cause drug-induced lupus, with higher risk in slow acetylators.
Methyldopa, an antihypertensive used in pregnancy, is a recognized cause of drug-induced lupus and also of autoimmune hemolytic anemia.

entries.changeSummary: Replaced 'Procainamide' with 'Minocycline' so the group is not given away by the hydralazine and procainamide pair.
entries.checkNote: Minocycline is a well-established drug-induced lupus cause; p-ANCA note is accurate.

check.note: Minocycline is a well-established drug-induced lupus cause; p-ANCA note is accurate.

entries.subject: MSK

original.title: Sjogren diagnostic clues
original.explanation: Autoimmune exocrine-gland injury produces dry eyes and mouth, reduced tear production, and focal lymphocytic sialadenitis on minor salivary gland biopsy.

entries.source: Bootcamp.com MSK.pdf; Rheumatologic Diseases / Sjogren syndrome; PDF pp. 29

proposal.title: Sjogren syndrome clues
proposal.why: Removes the redundant dry-eye test and adds a certain, classic extraglandular Sjogren association that demands recall and tempts toward renal categories.
proposal.changes: Replace 'Reduced Schirmer tear production' with 'Distal (type 1) RTA'; title broadened from diagnostic clues to clues.

entries.auditNote: Dry eyes plus dry mouth is instant Sjogren, and keratoconjunctivitis sicca and reduced Schirmer production are essentially the same clue twice.

revised.title: Sjogren syndrome clues
revised.explanation: Each is a characteristic glandular or extraglandular feature of Sjogren syndrome, an autoimmune lymphocytic destruction of exocrine glands.
revised.detail: Lymphocytic infiltration of lacrimal and salivary glands causes dry eyes (keratoconjunctivitis sicca) and dry mouth (xerostomia), and minor salivary gland biopsy shows focal lymphocytic sialadenitis. Extraglandular disease includes interstitial nephritis with distal renal tubular acidosis, along with anti-Ro/SSA and anti-La/SSB antibodies and increased risk of B-cell lymphoma. Distal RTA also occurs with other causes, such as amphotericin B and hypercalciuria, so the tile needs the other clues to place it.
tileNotes: Keratoconjunctivitis sicca is dry eye from lymphocytic destruction of lacrimal glands, a core Sjogren feature.
Xerostomia is dry mouth from salivary gland destruction, causing dental caries and difficulty swallowing dry food.
Tubulointerstitial nephritis in Sjogren syndrome can impair distal acid secretion, causing distal (type 1) renal tubular acidosis.
Minor salivary gland biopsy shows focal lymphocytic sialadenitis, scored by focus score in the classification criteria.

entries.changeSummary: Replaced 'Reduced Schirmer tear production' (a second dry-eye clue) with 'Distal (type 1) RTA' and broadened the title from diagnostic clues to clues.
entries.checkNote: Distal RTA is a classic extraglandular Sjogren feature; content accurate.

check.note: Distal RTA is a classic extraglandular Sjogren feature; content accurate.

entries.subject: MSK

original.title: Characteristic limited systemic sclerosis features
original.explanation: Four components of the classic CREST phenotype of limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis. Esophageal dysmotility is the fifth (omitted) component; not all features need be present simultaneously.

entries.source: Bootcamp.com MSK.pdf; Rheumatologic Diseases / Scleroderma; PDF pp. 37

proposal.why: Breaks the CREST letter pattern with the certain, characteristic serologic marker of limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis.

entries.auditNote: Four letters of CREST; the mnemonic makes the group and its missing E immediate.

revised.title: Characteristic limited systemic sclerosis features
revised.explanation: Each is a characteristic clinical or serologic feature of limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis.
revised.detail: Limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis restricts skin thickening to the fingers, distal limbs, and face and shows the CREST phenotype: calcinosis, Raynaud phenomenon, esophageal dysmotility, sclerodactyly, and telangiectasias. Anti-centromere antibodies are its characteristic serologic marker and are linked to later pulmonary arterial hypertension. Diffuse cutaneous disease instead involves the trunk and proximal limbs, with anti-Scl-70 (topoisomerase I) or anti-RNA polymerase III antibodies and earlier lung and renal involvement.
tileNotes: Calcinosis cutis is subcutaneous calcium deposition, often in the fingertips, and is the C of CREST.
Raynaud phenomenon is episodic digital vasospasm and is usually the earliest feature of limited systemic sclerosis.
Sclerodactyly is skin thickening and tightening of the fingers, the S of CREST.
Anti-centromere antibodies are the characteristic autoantibody of limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis, in contrast to anti-Scl-70 in diffuse disease.

entries.changeSummary: Replaced 'Telangiectasias' with 'Anti-centromere antibodies' to break the CREST letter pattern.
entries.checkNote: Anti-centromere is the characteristic limited SSc antibody and breaks the CREST pattern.

check.note: Anti-centromere is the characteristic limited SSc antibody and breaks the CREST pattern.

entries.subject: MSK

original.title: Sarcoidosis diagnostic associations
original.explanation: These findings support sarcoidosis after exclusion of other granulomatous disorders. Serum ACE and the elevated bronchoalveolar lavage CD4:CD8 ratio have limited sensitivity and specificity and are not required.

entries.source: Bootcamp.com MSK.pdf; Rheumatologic Diseases / Sarcoidosis; PDF pp. 38

proposal.why: Elevated ACE is a single-disease giveaway; hypercalcemia (granuloma 1-alpha-hydroxylase activity) is a certain sarcoid association that tempts toward hyperparathyroidism and malignancy categories.

entries.auditNote: Bilateral hilar adenopathy, noncaseating granulomas and elevated ACE form the textbook sarcoid triad.

revised.title: Sarcoidosis diagnostic associations
revised.explanation: Each is a classic finding that supports sarcoidosis, a multisystem disease of noncaseating granulomas diagnosed after other causes are excluded.
revised.detail: Sarcoidosis most often involves the lungs and hilar lymph nodes, and biopsy shows noncaseating granulomas. Activated granuloma macrophages express 1-alpha-hydroxylase, producing calcitriol and causing hypercalcemia or hypercalciuria. Bronchoalveolar lavage typically shows lymphocytosis with an increased CD4:CD8 ratio. Hypercalcemia also occurs in primary hyperparathyroidism (high PTH) and malignancy, but in sarcoidosis PTH is suppressed and calcitriol is high, and granulomas are present.
tileNotes: Bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy is the most common chest radiograph finding in sarcoidosis.
Noncaseating epithelioid granulomas on biopsy are the histologic hallmark, though other granulomatous diseases must be excluded.
Granuloma macrophages express 1-alpha-hydroxylase and convert 25-hydroxyvitamin D to calcitriol, causing PTH-independent hypercalcemia.
Bronchoalveolar lavage in sarcoidosis typically shows lymphocytosis with an elevated CD4:CD8 ratio.

entries.changeSummary: Replaced 'Elevated serum ACE' with 'Hypercalcemia' to break the textbook sarcoid triad.

fixes.detail: Sarcoidosis most often involves the lungs and hilar lymph nodes, and biopsy shows noncaseating granulomas. Activated granuloma macrophages express 1-alpha-hydroxylase, producing calcitriol and causing hypercalcemia or hypercalciuria. Bronchoalveolar lavage typically shows lymphocytosis with an increased CD4:CD8 ratio. Hypercalcemia also occurs in primary hyperparathyroidism (high PTH) and malignancy, but in sarcoidosis PTH is suppressed and calcitriol is high, and granulomas are present.

entries.subject: MSK

original.title: Giant cell arteritis cranial clues
original.explanation: In an older patient, cranial ischemic symptoms with compatible temporal artery histology support GCA; visual symptoms warrant urgent high-dose glucocorticoids. Biopsy can miss skip lesions.

entries.source: Bootcamp.com MSK.pdf; Vasculitides / Giant cell arteritis; PDF pp. 69

proposal.changes: Replace 'Temporal artery giant-cell inflammation' with 'Scalp tenderness'.

revised.title: Giant cell arteritis cranial clues
revised.explanation: Each is a classic cranial symptom of giant cell arteritis, reflecting inflammation and ischemia in branches of the external and internal carotid arteries.
revised.detail: Giant cell arteritis is a granulomatous vasculitis of large and medium arteries in patients over 50. Involvement of the superficial temporal artery causes new headache and scalp tenderness, facial artery involvement causes jaw claudication, and ophthalmic or posterior ciliary artery involvement causes transient or permanent vision loss. Visual symptoms call for immediate high-dose glucocorticoids before biopsy. GCA is closely linked with polymyalgia rheumatica, which causes proximal girdle stiffness rather than cranial ischemic symptoms.
tileNotes: A new headache, often temporal, in a patient over 50 is the most common symptom of giant cell arteritis.
Jaw claudication, pain in the jaw muscles with chewing, reflects ischemia from facial or maxillary artery involvement and is among the most specific GCA symptoms.
Transient monocular vision loss (amaurosis fugax) from ophthalmic or posterior ciliary artery ischemia can precede permanent blindness.
Scalp tenderness, for example when combing hair, reflects inflammation of the superficial temporal and occipital arteries.

entries.subject: MSK

original.title: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis clues
original.explanation: The upper-airway, pulmonary, renal, and PR3-ANCA pattern is characteristic of GPA. PR3-ANCA is not universal and renal involvement or cavitation may be absent.

entries.source: Bootcamp.com MSK.pdf; Vasculitides / GPA; PDF pp. 77

proposal.why: Replacing the serologic giveaway with a certain GPA upper-airway finding forces discrimination from relapsing polychondritis, cocaine use and other ANCA vasculitides.

revised.title: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis clues
revised.explanation: Each is a classic upper airway, pulmonary, or renal feature of granulomatosis with polyangiitis.
revised.detail: GPA is a necrotizing granulomatous vasculitis of small and medium vessels with a classic triad of upper airway, lung, and kidney involvement, usually with PR3-ANCA (c-ANCA). Upper airway disease causes chronic sinusitis and destruction of nasal cartilage (saddle nose). Lung involvement causes nodules that cavitate, and kidney involvement is a pauci-immune crescentic glomerulonephritis. Microscopic polyangiitis lacks granulomas and upper airway destruction, and eosinophilic GPA features asthma and eosinophilia.
tileNotes: Granulomatous destruction of nasal septal cartilage in GPA causes saddle nose deformity; relapsing polychondritis, cocaine use, and congenital syphilis are other causes.
Chronic sinusitis and other upper airway inflammation are the most common presenting features of GPA.
Necrotizing granulomas in the lungs produce multiple nodules that often cavitate.
GPA kidney involvement is a pauci-immune (few or no immune deposits) crescentic glomerulonephritis.

entries.subject: Renal

original.title: Thiazide and thiazide-like diuretics
original.explanation: These drugs inhibit the Na-Cl cotransporter (NCC) in the early distal convoluted tubule and reduce urinary calcium excretion.

entries.source: Bootcamp.com Nephrology.pdf; Renal Pharmacology > Thiazide Diuretics (PDF pp. 33, 43, 117, 118)

proposal.why: Indapamide is a certain thiazide-like NCC inhibitor; swapping out chlorothiazide removes one title leak and one 'chlor' stem.

entries.auditNote: Two tiles contain 'thiazide' from the title and three share 'chlor', giving the group away by spelling.

revised.title: Thiazide and thiazide-like diuretics
revised.explanation: Each drug inhibits the Na-Cl cotransporter (NCC) in the early distal convoluted tubule.
revised.detail: Hydrochlorothiazide is a thiazide, while chlorthalidone, indapamide, and metolazone are thiazide-like diuretics that share the same target despite different chemical structures. Blocking NCC causes modest natriuresis, decreases urinary calcium excretion, and can cause hypokalemia, hyponatremia, hyperglycemia, hyperlipidemia, and hyperuricemia. Metolazone remains effective at low GFR and is often combined with loop diuretics. Loop diuretics act on NKCC2 and increase urinary calcium, and potassium-sparing diuretics act in the collecting duct.
tileNotes: Hydrochlorothiazide is the prototypical thiazide diuretic, inhibiting NCC in the distal convoluted tubule.
Indapamide is a thiazide-like diuretic that inhibits NCC and is used for hypertension.
Chlorthalidone is a long-acting thiazide-like diuretic that inhibits NCC.
Metolazone is a thiazide-like diuretic that inhibits NCC and stays effective at reduced GFR, so it is often added to loop diuretics.

entries.changeSummary: Replaced 'Chlorothiazide' with 'Indapamide', removing one title-word tile and one 'chlor' stem.
entries.checkNote: Indapamide is a standard thiazide-like NCC inhibitor; content accurate.
